summary: P0 guest persistence fix verified. All 10 tests passed (5 new + 5 regression). Same device_id → same user_id (atomic upsert). Usage count of 3 survived logout + re-auth (no reset). 5 concurrent /api/auth/guest with same device_id produced EXACTLY 1 users document in MongoDB (partial unique index + find_one_and_update upsert holding). Empty body fallback works. Regression: admin login, /auth/me, /ai/tool smart_reply (3 suggestions), /tts nova & coral all 200 OK.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /auth/guest implementation is correct: atomic find_one_and_update with upsert + $setOnInsert ensures only one document per device_id; $set updates last_seen_at on every call.

Startup hook order is correct: _dedupe_guest_users() runs BEFORE create_index('guest_device_id', unique=True, partialFilter) — prevents the unique index creation from failing on legacy duplicate data.

Partial filter expression {is_guest: true, guest_device_id: {$type: 'string'}} correctly scopes uniqueness only to guest users with a string device id, so admin/google users (no guest_device_id) and legacy fallback guests (no guest_device_id field) are unaffected.

_user_public computes tool_uses_today from tool_usage_count only when tool_usage_date == today — so daily resets at UTC midnight still work, while same-day persistence is preserved across sessions. Verified live: post-logout re-auth returned tool_uses_today=3.

Minor observation (not a bug): /auth/guest mints a NEW session_token on every call (even when user already exists). This is intentional and matches the test expectations, but it does mean stale sessions accumulate in user_sessions until expires_at (30 days). Consider a cleanup job in future iterations — out of scope for this P0 fix.
seed_data_creation: Test creates and tears down 3 guest device docs (TEST_DEVICE_PERSIST_001, TEST_DEVICE_USAGE_002, TEST_DEVICE_RACE_003) via an autouse cleanup fixture that wipes both users + user_sessions before and after each test. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter13 fix locked in. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter13_guest_persistence.py is reusable as a regression suite — covers atomic upsert, race protection (5 concurrent threads + direct MongoDB doc count), usage persistence across logout, no-device-id fallback, and core regression (admin login, smart_reply, tts nova/coral). For future guest-related changes, re-run this file first.
rca_of_issue: Root cause (already fixed by main agent): The previous /api/auth/guest implementation issued an insert per call without a unique index on guest_device_id. Concurrent requests during app cold-start / sign-out / reinstall created multiple guest user documents for the same physical device, each with its own tool_usage_count=0. Subsequent /auth/me calls landed on a different duplicate doc and read 0 — making the daily limit appear to reset. Fix: (1) atomic find_one_and_update with upsert returns the same survivor doc for any concurrent caller; (2) partial unique index on {is_guest:true, guest_device_id} guarantees Mongo rejects any race-stragglers; (3) startup _dedupe_guest_users() merges any legacy duplicates, keeping the doc with the highest same-day tool_usage_count and re-pointing sessions to the survivor before the unique index is built. Validated end-to-end: race test fires 5 simultaneous calls with same device_id, asserts exactly 1 doc in DB and all callers received the same user_id.
